authorization_probe.request_scope: Anonymous request with public official CLI client ID, response_type=code, openid offline_access, unused loopback callback, fresh random PKCE challenge and state; no cookies, no token exchange, no redirects followed.

cli_comparison.auth_command_note: auth login/status/logout was added on main October 14, after v0.3.0. auth is not supported by either installed release; this explains the command mismatch, not the empty download.
cli_comparison.callback_response: Both v0.2.0 and v0.3.0, and inspected main, explicitly send HTTP 200 and Content-Type: text/html with the Authentication Successful page from localhost /callback.

conclusion.established: The valid CLI authorization request is rate-limited upstream, before any redirect to the localhost callback. Credential refresh independently returned HTTP 429 in earlier retained diagnostics.
conclusion.inference: The empty auth download is consistent with this zero-byte authorization response, whose path ends in auth and lacks a Content-Type. The exact browser network response has not been independently captured.
not_established: Which tenant, application, IP or account shares the exhausted limit.
That the website hotfix caused the rate limit.
That changing the CLI version resolves this server-side response.
